Generate mock splice events in a GRanges object

Source: R/mock_data.R
generate_events.Rd

Functions to introduce specific types of alternative splicing events into mock GRanges data for testing purposes.

Each generator edits the transcripts on one side and marks, in a logical sim_event column, the exons the matching finder should report. generate_se(), generate_cse(), generate_ri(), generate_a5ss(), generate_a3ss(), generate_atss() and generate_ates() edit up (positive estimate) transcripts. generate_ie(), generate_cie() and generate_si() are their mirrors: the same edit made to a down (negative estimate) transcript. generate_mxe() edits one transcript on each side.

Usage

generate_se(gr, n_events = 1)

generate_ie(gr, n_events = 1)

generate_cse(gr, n_events = 1, n_skip = 2)

generate_cie(gr, n_events = 1, n_skip = 2)

generate_mxe(gr, n_events = 1)

generate_ri(gr, n_events = 1)

generate_si(gr, n_events = 1)

generate_a5ss(gr, n_events = 1)

generate_a3ss(gr, n_events = 1)

generate_atss(gr, n_events = 1, mode = c("shift", "drop"))

generate_ates(gr, n_events = 1, mode = c("shift", "drop"))

Arguments

gr

A GRanges object with metadata columns: 'exon_rank', 'gene_id', 'tx_id', and 'estimate'.

n_events

Number of events to generate, i.e. the number of genes that get one. Every generator puts at most one event in a gene, so two events never edit the same transcripts. When fewer genes than n_events have a candidate, it warns and makes one in each of those.

n_skip

Number of consecutive exons skipped (or included) together, at least 2. Every exon of the run is internal, so a transcript needs at least n_skip + 2 exons to host one.

mode

How to move the site: "shift" moves the terminal exon's outer boundary (so it still overlaps its partner), "drop" removes the terminal exon and re-ranks (so the new terminal exon does not overlap its partner at all).

Value

generate_se(): A GRanges object with skipped exon events introduced: an internal exon is removed from one up transcript per gene

generate_ie(): A GRanges object with included exon events introduced: an internal exon is removed from one down transcript per gene, so the up transcripts include it

generate_cse(): A GRanges object with consecutive skipped exon events introduced: a run of n_skip internal exons is removed from one up transcript per gene

generate_cie(): A GRanges object with consecutive included exon events introduced: a run of n_skip internal exons is removed from one down transcript per gene, so the up transcripts include it

generate_mxe(): A GRanges object with mutually exclusive exon events introduced: a down transcript loses internal exon k + 1 and an up transcript of the same gene loses exon k, so each keeps the exon the other lacks. One pair per gene.

generate_ri(): A GRanges object with retained intron events introduced: exons 2 and 3 of one up transcript per gene are fused

generate_si(): A GRanges object with spliced intron events introduced: exons 2 and 3 of one down transcript per gene are fused, so the up transcripts splice out the intron it retains

generate_a5ss(): A GRanges object with alternative 5' splice site events introduced: the donor of an internal exon is moved by 2 bp in one up transcript per gene

generate_a3ss(): A GRanges object with alternative 3' splice site events introduced: the acceptor of an internal exon is moved by 2 bp in one up transcript per gene

generate_atss(): A GRanges object with alternative transcription start site events introduced: the first exon of one up transcript per gene is shortened at its outer end ("shift") or removed ("drop")

generate_ates(): A GRanges object with alternative transcription end site events introduced: the last exon of one up transcript per gene is shortened at its outer end ("shift") or removed ("drop")

Examples


gr <- create_mock_data(
  n_genes = 2, n_tx_per_gene = 4, n_exons_per_tx = 4
)
generate_se(gr, n_events = 1)
#> GRanges object with 31 ranges and 8 metadata columns:
#>        seqnames    ranges strand |   gene_id     tx_id exon_rank  estimate
#>           <Rle> <IRanges>  <Rle> | <integer> <numeric> <integer> <numeric>
#>    [1]     chr7       1-5      + |         1         1         1  -0.35974
#>    [2]     chr7     11-15      + |         1         1         2  -0.35974
#>    [3]     chr7     21-25      + |         1         1         3  -0.35974
#>    [4]     chr7     31-35      + |         1         1         4  -0.35974
#>    [5]     chr7       1-5      + |         1         2         1   0.75178
#>    ...      ...       ...    ... .       ...       ...       ...       ...
#>   [27]     chr7   121-125      + |         2         7         4  0.105800
#>   [28]     chr7     91-95      + |         2         8         1 -0.561528
#>   [29]     chr7   101-105      + |         2         8         2 -0.561528
#>   [30]     chr7   111-115      + |         2         8         3 -0.561528
#>   [31]     chr7   121-125      + |         2         8         4 -0.561528
#>                key    nexons  internal sim_event
#>        <character> <integer> <logical> <logical>
#>    [1]         1-1         4     FALSE     FALSE
#>    [2]         1-2         4      TRUE      TRUE
#>    [3]         1-3         4      TRUE     FALSE
#>    [4]         1-4         4     FALSE     FALSE
#>    [5]         2-1         3     FALSE     FALSE
#>    ...         ...       ...       ...       ...
#>   [27]         7-4         4     FALSE     FALSE
#>   [28]         8-1         4     FALSE     FALSE
#>   [29]         8-2         4      TRUE     FALSE
#>   [30]         8-3         4      TRUE     FALSE
#>   [31]         8-4         4     FALSE     FALSE
#>   -------
#>   seqinfo: 1 sequence from an unspecified genome; no seqlengths
